svg.title: From layout edges to neighbour slots
svg.desc: Animated: PoseGraph classifies each edge of W8 for pose (W8, 90°) by the bearing of the edge relative to the yaw: W31 LEFT, W9 RIGHT, W4 BACK, W13 FORWARD, each within 0.1 rad. Then three hypothetical edits: a diagonal edge that throws, a disallowed_edge_orientation that removes heading 90 and -90 from edge 8-13, and a 0.1 m misalignment that PoseGraph accepts but GetMotionType rejects.
svg.metadata: ["Pose (W8, 90\u00b0): W8 at heading 90\u00b0. PoseGraph measures each edge against yaw = 90\u00b0 \u00d7 pi/180 = pi/2 rad in the atan2 frame (0 = +x, counter-clockwise), which points to +y. The four wedges are the translation slots: FORWARD at relative bearing 0, LEFT at +pi/2, BACK at pi, RIGHT at \u2212pi/2, each \u00b10.1 rad (5.7\u00b0) wide. The yaw used as a math angle points out of the AGV's right side, not its front: the AGV faces \u2212x, so LEFT is the AGV's forward, RIGHT its back, FORWARD its right and BACK its left. All eight slots start at -1 (kInvalidIndex).", "Neighbour W31 (28.0253, 12.7753) also allows heading 90\u00b0, so pose (W31, 90\u00b0) exists. dx = -2.857, dy = 0: bearing atan2(0, -2.857) = 180\u00b0; relative to the yaw: +90\u00b0, inside the LEFT wedge. Slot LEFT (3) = (W31, 90\u00b0): the AGV's forward, a locomote toward the approach of bay B7.", "Neighbour W9 (37.1856, 12.7753): dx = +6.3033, dy = 0, bearing 0\u00b0, relative \u221290\u00b0: RIGHT (1) = (W9, 90\u00b0), the AGV's back, the other locomote direction.", "Neighbour W4 (30.8823, 10.4893): dx = 0, dy = -2.286, bearing \u221290\u00b0, relative \u2212180\u00b0, the same angle as +180\u00b0: BACK (2) = (W4, 90\u00b0), the AGV's left, a strafe.", "Neighbour W13 (30.8823, 17.1663): dy = +4.391, bearing +90\u00b0, relative 0\u00b0: FORWARD (0) = (W13, 90\u00b0), the AGV's right, a strafe. W8 has rotation_allowed, so ROT_RIGHT (4) = (W8, 0\u00b0) and ROT_LEFT (5) = (W8, 180\u00b0), the nearest headings clockwise and counter-clockwise; no VRC, so slots 6 and 7 stay -1. Pose (W8, \u221290\u00b0) gets the mirror image: FORWARD W4, RIGHT W31, BACK W13, LEFT W9.", "Hypothetical edge W8\u2013W5 (not in the YAML). Both nodes allow heading 90\u00b0, so the edge is classified: bearing atan2(-2.286, 6.3033) = \u221219.9\u00b0, relative \u2212109.9\u00b0, 19.9\u00b0 (0.35 rad) from RIGHT and outside every wedge. The PoseGraph constructor throws. Poses are built in node-id order, so pose (W5, \u221290\u00b0) gets there first and the message reads \"Edge 5 <-> 8 with invalid translation connection!\". Had the nodes shared no heading, the edge would be skipped without a word.", "Hypothetical disallowed_edge_orientation: 90 on edge W8\u2013W13. IsAngleOrReciprocal(90, heading) is true for 90\u00b0 and \u221290\u00b0, so (W8, 90\u00b0) loses FORWARD, (W8, \u221290\u00b0) loses BACK, and W13's poses lose W8. W13 has only those two headings, so the edge is gone from the PoseGraph while Layout::HasEdge(W8, 13\u00b0) stays true. W8\u2013W13 is the only edge between the two YAML sandboxes, so the pose graph would split in two.", "Hypothetical: W31 moved 0.1 m north (y = 12.8753). Bearing 178.0\u00b0, relative +88.0\u00b0: still inside the 5.7\u00b0 LEFT wedge, so PoseGraph builds the edge. GetMotionType checks the same edge with IsLocomoteOrStrafe at 1e-3 rad: 2.0\u00b0 (0.035 rad) is neither a locomote nor a strafe, and it throws \"Edge traversal is not perpendicular to where we are.\" on the first command that uses it.", "The complete picture: the four Pecos edges of W8 fill slots 0 to 3 of (W8, 90\u00b0), rotation fills 4 and 5. Three rules to remember when editing edges: an off-axis edge throws only when the two nodes share a heading; a disallowed orientation removes a heading and its reciprocal from one edge; and PoseGraph's 0.1 rad tolerance is 100 times looser than the 1e-3 rad of GetMotionType."]

g.text: The YAML edges are undirected and carry no direction names. PoseGraph gives them names per pose: it takes the atan2 bearing of each edge, subtracts the pose's yaw and snaps the result to one of four slots, within 0.1 rad. Step through the four
